findings.claim: The serializer method `include_website_name` lacks the trailing `?` that ActiveModel::Serializer requires for `include_<attr>?` predicates. As a result it is never called and `website_name` is always serialized, as null when there is no website.

verifier.reason: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 defines `include_website_name` without `?`, while the pinned AMS 0.8.3 (Gemfile.lock:22) only looks up `include_<attr>?` (the form used at user_serializer.rb:9,18,27 and lib/plugin/instance.rb:61), so the predicate is dead code and `website_name` is always emitted, as nil when the host is nil (user_serializer.rb:140). The AMS gem source is not vendored here, so the lookup rule rests on known 0.8.x behaviour and the repo's own convention.

findings.claim: UserSerializer's `website_name` does not honor `Guardian#restrict_user_fields?` and is not in `untrusted_attributes`, unlike `website`. This exposes the website host/path of TL0 users to anonymous viewers.

verifier.reason: `website_name` is added as a plain attribute (app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:43) but is absent from `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111), and its only guard is `include_website_name` without the `?` (line 153), which the serializer never calls and which does not check `restrict_user_fields?` anyway. The method reads `object.user_profile.website` directly (lines 133-151), so an anonymous viewer of a TL0 user gets the website host (plus path when the domain matches the forum's) even though `website` itself is hidden.

findings.claim: The sibling-subdomain branch of `website_name` treats any hosts with the same label count (>2) and equal labels after the first as the same site, even across public suffixes. For example, `evil.co.uk` matches `forum.co.uk` and `a.github.io` matches `forum.github.io`, so the full path is shown for unrelated sites.

verifier.reason: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:144-146 only checks that both hosts have the same label count (>2) and identical labels after the first, with no public-suffix awareness. So `evil.co.uk` vs `forum.co.uk` and `a.github.io` vs `forum.github.io` both compare equal (`co.uk`, `github.io`) and return host + path for unrelated sites.

findings.claim: Tests are missing for the sibling-subdomain branch, nil/blank website, the unparseable-URI rescue path, the www-vs-apex case, and the TL0/anonymous restriction on `website_name`.

verifier.reason: spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:76-91 has only three `website_name` cases (unrelated host, same host, parent of instance host), so the sibling-subdomain `elsif` at app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:144-146, the nil/blank and URI-rescue paths at :138-140, and www-vs-apex are never exercised. The TL0/anonymous spec list at spec:11 omits `website_name`, which is in fact not restricted at all: it is absent from `untrusted_attributes` (serializer :105-111) and `include_website_name` at :153 lacks the `?`.

findings.claim: No spec covers a nil or blank website, including checking that `website_name` is absent or nil.

verifier.reason: The only specs touching `website_name` are in the "with filled out website" context (spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:67-92), all with website set to 'http://example.com/user'; no spec sets a nil or blank website or asserts `website_name` is nil or absent, and the TL0 untrusted-attributes list at line 11 omits `website_name`. A repo-wide search finds `website_name` in no other spec file.

findings.claim: No spec covers the sibling-subdomain branch (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`).

verifier.reason: The only `website_name` specs (spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:77-89) use website `http://example.com/user` with hostnames `discourse.org`, `example.com` and `forums.example.com`; these hit the equality branch and the `else` branch only. The sibling-subdomain `elsif` at app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:143-145 needs both hosts to have the same number of labels and more than two, which no spec sets up.

findings.claim: The host comparison in `website_name` is case-sensitive because URI#host preserves case and nothing downcases it. So `http://Example.com/u` does not match instance `example.com`.

verifier.reason: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:138-149 compares `URI(website.to_s).host` to `Discourse.current_hostname` with `==` and `ends_with?` and never downcases either side; Ruby's `URI#host` keeps the original case, and the stored website is not normalised on save (app/services/user_updater.rb:105-107 only prepends `http://`). So `http://Example.com/u` on instance `example.com` falls to the else branch and returns just `Example.com` without the path.

findings.claim: For a same-domain URL with path `/`, `website_name` renders `example.com/`. The port is also silently dropped, so `example.com:8080/u` shows as `example.com/u`.

verifier.reason: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:137-150 builds the name as `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`; `URI#host` excludes the port and `URI#path` is `/` for `http://example.com/`, so the results are `example.com/` and `example.com/u` (the removed JS `website.split("/")[2]` kept the port). Read from the code, not executed.

findings.claim: Same-domain matching in `website_name` is asymmetric. With website `http://www.example.com/u` on instance `example.com`, the check runs in the wrong direction (`'example.com'.ends_with?('.www.example.com')`) and shows only the host without the path, while the reverse case shows the path.

verifier.reason: In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:147-149 the else branch only tests `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`, so website `www.example.com` on instance `example.com` (segment counts 3 vs 2, skipping line 144) evaluates `'example.com'.ends_with?('.www.example.com')` → false and returns host only. The reverse case (website `example.com`, instance `www.example.com`) returns host plus path.

findings.claim: The client-side computed websiteName that tracked `model.website` was replaced by a server-computed `model.website_name` that is set once. After a user edits their website in preferences, the profile shows a stale or missing website name until a full page reload.

verifier.reason: The profile header now reads `model.website_name` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/user/user.hbs:66-71), which is only populated by `findDetails` in the user route's `afterModel` (routes/user.js.es6:54, models/user.js.es6:320). `User.save` copies only `bio_excerpt` from the PUT response (models/user.js.es6:209-213), and preferences is nested under the user route (routes/app-route-map.js.es6:74), so the name stays stale or missing after a website edit until the user route is re-entered — not strictly a full page reload.

findings.claim: The preferences controller's `.then` refreshes only `name` and `bio_cooked` after saving, not `website_name`.

verifier.reason: The save `.then` at app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/preferences.js.es6:117-123 only sets the current user's `name` and `model.bio_cooked`, and `User#save` (models/user.js.es6:209-214) copies only `bio_excerpt` from the response, so `model.website_name` (now rendered in templates/user/user.hbs:66-71) stays stale after the website is edited. The patch removed the client-side `websiteName` computed property on `model.website` that previously updated automatically.

findings.claim: `User#save` copies back only `bio_excerpt` from the PUT response and ignores `website_name`, even though `users_controller#update` returns the full UserSerializer.

verifier.reason: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/user.js.es6:209-210 copies only `data.user.bio_excerpt` from the PUT response, though users_controller.rb:100 returns the full UserSerializer (now including `website_name`); since the patch replaced the client-side `websiteName` computed with server-supplied `model.website_name` (user.hbs:66-71), the profile header shows a stale website name after saving preferences until the user is reloaded.

findings.claim: The profile template gates rendering on `model.website_name` but uses `model.website` for the href/title. When `website` is omitted, it can render text with an empty or broken link.

verifier.reason: `website` is omitted for TL0 users viewed anonymously (`include_website?` at app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:25-32,109), but `website_name` is still serialized because its guard at user_serializer.rb:153 is named `include_website_name` without the `?` and never checks `restrict_user_fields?`. The template at app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/user/user.hbs:66-71 then shows the host name with an undefined `model.website`; in that case the user is TL0, so it renders the `<span>` with an empty title rather than a broken `<a>`, and exposes the hidden website host.

findings.claim: `website_name` parses `URI(website)` three times and calls `discourse_host.split('.')` four times, using nested ternaries.

verifier.reason: The redundancy is real, though the claim's counts are slightly off: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:138,143,146,149 call `URI(website.to_s)` four times (two per execution path) and lines 144 and 146 call `discourse_host.split('.')` three times. The ternaries at lines 146 and 149 sit inside if/elsif branches rather than being nested in each other; the effect is purely readability and minor wasted work, not behaviour.
